331 SHRI SURYABHAN PATIL VAHADANE: 
SHRI BRATIN SENGUPTA:  
Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the procedures followed in dispose of the Recurring Deposit

(b) the number of cases pending with the postal department in 
Delhi for the settlement of Recurring Deposits to the affected families

(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI RAM 
VILAS PASWAN): (a) to (d) The procedure for settlement of Recurring 
Deposit Scheme claims relating to missing persons is as under: 
• An application has to be made by the claimant to the 
Postmaster concerned. 
• Every claim is required to be supported by a probate of will, 
or letters of administration of  certificate granted under the 
Indian Succession Act, 1925. In  cases where the claimant 
does not produce any of the aforesaid legal evidence of heir-
ship, the following documents need to be obtained and 
forwarded to the Head of the Circle for issue of sanction. 
13 

RAJYA SABHA [ 12 December, 2000] 
• Individual affidavits or declarations sworn before a Magistrate 
from the claimant and all the other near relatives of the 
depositor, indicating the facts and the date of disappearance and 
establishing that the person has not been heard of since or for 
more than seven years prior to the date of the claim preferred 
and; 
• Written consent statement from all the never relatives in 
favour of the claimant. 
• When the date of disapperance is not known, the date after 
the completion of seven years from the date on which the 
person was reported to be missing is taken as the dale of his 
death. 
• In cases where legal evidence of heir-ship is not produced, 
sanction 
can be issued provided the claimant is prepared to indemnify 
the 
Government against any adverse claim.

† 2525. SHRI RAJIV RANJAN SINGH "LALAN': 
SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that several big dams in the country have been 
constructed or are under construction; 
(b) if so, the total number of such dams at present; 
(c) the storage capacity of water reservoirs of such dams; 
(d) the total areas of land being used for storage; and 
(e) the percentage of this land out of the present irrigated land in the 
country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRTMATI BIJOYA CHAKRAVARTY): (a)to(c) As per 
information available, there are 3596 completed and 695 dams under construction in 
the country with a total live storage capacity of 249.15 billion cubic metre. 
(d) and (e) As per land use statistics of Ministry of Agriculture available 
at present, the net irrigated land in the country during 1996-97 is 55.143 
million hectare. An area of 4.79 million hectare of land is being utilised for 
storage in 2611 large dam" for which information is available in the 
National Register.
